phases.name: Remove live Exec contracts and execution
phases.description: Baseline: 37 production Rust files contain affected symbols; six steps give a 0.16 decomposition ratio. Configuration-only disabling removes none of the compatibility surface; scalar-driver collapse violates the retained registry contract.

steps.name: Cut admission, probes, and archived intent to VM
steps.description: Atomically remove Exec admission and host-command probing, preserve HTTP/TCP probing, delete the public Exec accessor, and reset the affected Service-spec and workload-intent envelopes to current VM-only V1.
criteria: Valid VM Job, Service, and Schedule TOML plus HTTP request/description values preserve workload kind and complete typed payloads through roundtrip.
Missing supported-driver input and generated unsupported driver keys use existing generic parser/serde behavior; invalid VM HTTP submission writes no intent.
VM HTTP/TCP probes retain target, role/index, thresholds, result publication, cancellation, re-registration, and the existing Earned-Trust boot gate.
Current VM-only Service specifications and all three workload-intent kinds roundtrip through their new sole V1 envelopes.
No old reader, fixture, compatibility diagnostic, guest-probe placeholder, or replacement for WorkloadSpecInput::exec_command remains; unrelated envelopes stay unchanged.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, Rust adaptation): retain the authored unsupported-key proptest with exact `/// CONTRACT_SHAPE: pure-function.`; bounded-change tests declare intent/probe universes and assert unchanged complements. Unit examples require `// bypass:`; integration remains single-example wiring evidence. Probe-algebra and driver-input changes share archived payloads, so atomically reset ServiceSpecEnvelope and WorkloadIntentEnvelope. Delete dedicated parser/probe/codec/accessor tests with their subjects; add no removed-name, source-shape, trybuild, compile-pass, old-byte, or absence test. Follow ADR-0110/0111/0113 exactly.

steps.name: Delete ExecDriver and production composition
steps.description: Delete the concrete host-process driver, export, composition helper, dedicated worker tests, and its netns error while preserving optional VM capability composition, registry/index ownership, and per-composed-driver exit observation.
criteria: One server boot yields registry empty on ordinary VMM absence, {Vm} on successful probe, and startup refusal on present-but-failing VMM capability.
A composed VM allocation receives the boot-trusted probe runner; guest exit publishes VM provenance and releases its supervision claim.
Server shutdown remains bounded and clean for empty and VM-populated registries without losing VM exit publication or supervision release.
No concrete host-process driver is exported or composed, and its dedicated production code and tests disappear in the same commit.
Driver, DriverRegistry, AllocDriverIndex, VmDriver, Vmm, and shared VM cgroup contracts remain unchanged.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, Rust adaptation): pure tests remain proptest properties; bounded production-boundary tests cover registry outcomes, trusted-runner delivery, VM exit publication/provenance, supervision release, and clean shutdown. Integration/Tier-3 stays single-example. EXEMPT FROM NEW PROPERTY: deletion adds no behavior. Exact observer-task cardinality, shared-token identity, and join-all ownership are reviewer diff audit only; add no test seam, function, private import, or source-shape check. Delete driver and dedicated suites together; retain registry/index/observer ownership and VMM absence/probe semantics.

steps.name: Collapse runtime dispatch onto the VM path
steps.description: Remove the inactive Exec payload route and network branch, make the current VM TAP plan mandatory, and preserve P-105 successor-first dispatch plus Running-to-intercept-to-guest-command ordering.
criteria: Every admitted allocation receives the current netns, veth, TAP, address, MAC, gateway, prefix, and DNS plan before VM start.
Accepted Running follows VM guest readiness; successful interception follows Running and precedes guest-command release.
Interception failure after Running writes the existing dominating Failed result, withholds guest-command release, and completes existing cleanup.
RestartAllocation retains the accepted predecessor ID, distinct durably reserved successor, successor-first result precedence, and one exact-old cleanup attempt.
The runtime payload has only VM; current VM network fields remain and no shared-switch, per-tap, shared-DNS, or replacement-mTLS mechanism appears.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, Rust adaptation): preserve the P-105 proptests and exact `/// CONTRACT_SHAPE: pure-function.` lines; bounded-change tests declare network, rows, interception, release, successor, predecessor, and cleanup universes with unchanged complements. Integration/Tier-3 tests remain single-example wiring evidence. Implement only the feature-delta shapes: non-optional VmTapPlan provisioning/injection, no network-assignment predicate, AllocationAttemptEvent::Dispatch, and guest_command_release_permitted. Private renames receive no shape test. Leave the schedule-racy P-105 oracle untouched and outside evidence. #295 is constraint-only.

phases.name: Reset lifecycle evidence and operator artifacts
phases.description: Reset the remaining Exec-coupled lifecycle vocabulary and two envelope owners, then migrate current operator documentation/examples without rewriting historical records or implementing #295.

steps.name: Reset lifecycle evidence to current V1
steps.description: Delete Exec-only driver/start/reason vocabulary, migrate surviving consumers to VM or generic variants, and atomically reset allocation-status and lifecycle-occurrence envelopes to their new current V1 baselines.
criteria: Surviving VM and generic start, crash, stop, cgroup, stderr, OOM, and internal-error evidence retains current rendering and lifecycle behavior.
Current allocation-status and lifecycle-occurrence payloads roundtrip through their new sole V1 envelopes using surviving source and reason vocabulary.
Exactly those two lifecycle envelopes reset; all unrelated observation, CA, workflow, probe, and service-backend envelope fixtures remain byte-identical.
Generated OpenAPI reflects the reduced current driver/reason/source vocabulary without aliases or deprecated spellings.
VM exits retain VM source, lifecycle publication, supervision release, and clean bounded server shutdown.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, Rust adaptation): pure lifecycle tests remain proptest properties; production-boundary tests cover VM exit provenance/publication, lifecycle rows, supervision release, and clean shutdown. Exact observer-task cardinality, shared-token identity, and join-all ownership are reviewer diff audit only; add no test seam, function, private import, or source-shape check. EXEMPT FROM PROPERTY: reset only AllocStatusRowEnvelope and AllocLifecycleOccurrenceRowEnvelope with one current-V1 roundtrip each. Delete old fixtures/tests. Remove only DriverType::Exec, DriverStartClass::Exec/ExecStartFailure, and the five approved TransitionReason variants.

steps.name: Migrate current operator artifacts to microVMs
steps.description: Migrate current examples and product guidance to the supported microVM model, delete host-process-only examples, and retain the checked-in healthy VM Service journey that will drive E14.
criteria: Current supported examples, README, whitepaper, jobs, journeys, and persona guidance use VM/microVM execution; host-process-only examples are removed.
The checked-in healthy VM Service example remains operator-runnable and source-valid without a deleted-spelling absence check.
Current guidance preserves HTTP/TCP probes, P-105 allocation identity, and Running-to-intercept-to-guest-command ordering.
Historical ADR/evolution prose plus E06 and E08 receipts remain unchanged and are not presented as post-cut evidence.
No documentation or example claims shared switching, per-tap interception, shared-bridge DNS, replacement mTLS, cross-host routing, density, or throughput.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, Rust adaptation): no application logic or new test is added. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this step changes examples and current documentation; use existing structural validation for surviving VM requirements, not deleted-name tokens. Delete host-process-only examples; migrate general examples to existing VM artifact preparation. Update only active whitepaper claims. Do not rewrite historical ADR/evolution material or E06/E08, or add #295 claims. Paths are guidance; include only current artifacts whose active promise or runnable spec changes.

phases.name: Capture post-cut VM Service evidence
phases.description: Capture one post-cut black-box VM Service event after implementation review. E14 is a SHA-pinned receipt, not a recurring test; the single final DELIVER mutation gate runs separately after all step reviews.

steps.name: Capture E14 from the checked-in VM example
steps.description: Capture E14 through the checked-in healthy VM Service journey using the built default-feature binary on native metal, retaining only stakeholder-visible success and owned cleanup evidence.
criteria: E14 drives the checked-in healthy VM Service example through the built default-feature binary on native metal.
The capture records stakeholder-visible VM Service success and owned cleanup against the exact post-cut SHA.
E14 preserves actual commands, output, substrate, SHA, and dirty state without inline specs, Rust crate imports, test harnesses, or integration assertions.
E06 and E08 remain unchanged historical receipts and are not cited as proof of the post-cut implementation.
A different reviewer evaluates E14; the implementation/capture author does not mark its own evidence satisfied.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, Rust adaptation): no application test is added; earlier proptest/state-delta and integration steps own code contracts. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: E14 is one SHA-pinned black-box capture, not a recurring test. Drive only `examples/service-kind-vm-workloads/run-example.sh run healthy` through the built default-feature product on native metal. Do not recreate specs, invoke tests, import/link crates, duplicate integration assertions, overwrite E06/E08, or self-approve evidence. A permanent runner is optional.

excluded_patterns: new remove_*.rs, trybuild, compile-pass, compile-fail, source-token, source-shape, or absence-test fixtures
shared-switch, per-tap interception, shared-bridge DNS, replacement transparent-mTLS, or other GH #295 implementation
compatibility aliases, readers, fallbacks, disabled variants, retired-driver diagnostics, old envelope fixtures, or deleted-name/source-shape tests
the pre-existing schedule-racy P-105 oracle or any production fix for it

final_mutation_gate.runs_after: All six step reviews are approved and E14 has independent evidence review.
final_mutation_gate.command: cargo xtask lima run -- cargo xtask mutants --diff origin/main --features integration-tests
final_mutation_gate.pass_condition: Command exits 0; target/xtask/mutants-summary.json reports status=pass, kill_rate_pct>=80, and total_mutants/caught/missed/timeout/unviable counts.
final_mutation_gate.evidence: Retain the complete target/xtask/mutants-summary.json as structured final DELIVER evidence.
final_mutation_gate.constraints: Run once as the DELIVER-wave background exception, never per-step; do not modify exclusions without explicit approval.
